assumptions: MultiPLX's interaction model: the tube holds both assays' primers and their products.
Probe interactions are primer3's thal under the same conditions, which is an addition to MultiPLX rather than its output.
limits: Pairwise: an assay compatible with two others and not the third cannot be pooled, and the pair is named.
A missing amplicon leaves the two primer-product scores unmeasurable, and that is reported rather than passed.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which of these qPCR assays can be pooled in one reaction, and which pair clashes?

description: Can these qPCR assays share a tube? Every unordered pair is scored on MultiPLX's five primer-primer and primer-product interactions and, beyond MultiPLX, on each assay's hydrolysis PROBE against the other assay's oligos (primer3 thal) — a probe consumed by a neighbour's primer loses signal while the PCR works perfectly, which reads as poor efficiency and is blamed on the primers.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

assays.description: the assays to pool: one object per assay with `name`, `forward`, `reverse`, `probe` and `amplicon`. Wire `design_qpcr_assay` outputs here, or list them yourself. Without `amplicon` the two primer-product scores cannot be measured and say so.

conditions.description: salt, magnesium, dNTP and oligo concentrations plus the salt-correction method every interaction is measured in. Left unset it is filled from your reaction-conditions settings, and falls back to primer3's defaults when there are none. Advanced.

additives.description: DMSO and formamide, applied AFTER the nearest-neighbour Tm.

DMSOfactor.description: °C of Tm lost per % DMSO, as an explicit override. Supplying it WINS over `dmsoMethod`, and detaches the number from its citation.

dmsoMethod.description: which published DMSO depression sets the coefficient. Values: ahs01 (Ahsen et al. (2001) (0.75 °C per %)), mus81 (Musielski et al. (1981) (0.6 °C per %)), cul76 (Cullen and Bick (1976) (0.5 °C per %)), esc80 (Escara and Hutton (1980) (0.675 °C per %)).

fmd.description: formamide — percent when `fmdmethod` is 1, molar when it is 2.

fmdfactor.description: °C lost per % formamide (method 1). Papers report 0.6 to 0.72.

fmdmethod.description: 1 = linear % formamide (McConaughy 1969) · 2 = GC-dependent, molar (Blake & Delcourt 1996). Values: 1 (Linear %, McConaughy 1969), 2 (GC-dependent molar, Blake & Delcourt 1996).

method.description: which validated nearest-neighbour model and default buffer — santaLucia (pydna `tm_default`, Taq) or dbd (pydna `tm_dbd`, Phusion / Pfu-Sso7d). Values: santaLucia (SantaLucia (pydna tm_default, Taq)), dbd (DNA-binding domain (pydna tm_dbd, Phusion)).

nnTable.description: override the method's nearest-neighbour table; the buffer convention is unchanged.

saltcorr.description: Biopython salt-correction method 0–7 (0 = none). It moves the answer more than any other knob here: on a 24-mer at the Taq buffer the eight span 79.302 °C (method 0) to 66.009 °C (method 2).

selfcomp.description: both strands are one self-complementary oligo (the concentration term becomes dnac1 rather than dnac1 − dnac2/2).

stringency.description: whose cutoffs decide. `primer3` judges on the Tm limits calibrated for the engine that computes them, which is what the panel opens on; the other three are MultiPLX's own presets, verbatim from cmultiplx 1.4. Values: primer3 (primer3 limits (the engine's own)), high (MultiPLX high stringency), normal (MultiPLX normal), low (MultiPLX low).

name: check_qpcr_multiplex

compatible.description: assay names that clashed with nothing — the ones that can be pooled

conflicting.description: assay names involved in at least one clash

cutoffs.description: the cutoff set the verdicts were judged against, so a report says what it means by compatible

pairs.description: every unordered pair: its five MultiPLX scores, its probe interactions, the cutoffs it breaks, whether it is compatible, and why not in words

poolable.description: true when NO pair clashes, so the whole set can go in one tube. Branch a workflow on this rather than counting the rows
